construction.access_recipe: GET https://data.www.sbir.gov/mod_awarddatapublic_no_abstract/award_data_no_abstract.csv with a normal browser user agent, then read the CSV in chunks with pandas.read_csv(low_memory=False). Normalise phase to 1, 2 or 3, program to SBIR or STTR, parse award_year and award_amount after removing dollar signs and commas. Build the firm key in priority order: UEI, else DUNS, else upper-cased company name with legal suffixes stripped plus canonical USPS state. Keep firms whose earliest award record is a Phase I award with award_year 2005-2018 and whose four-year label window is closed by the maximum award year. Derive award_date from proposal_award_date when it falls inside the award_year federal fiscal year, otherwise use the fiscal year end because HHS does not publish proposal_award_date. Label by joining later Phase II records on firm key and agency with y < award_year <= y+4. Drop abstract and award_title from the released table.
construction.expected_size: 65 MB CSV as published by SBA (the with-abstracts variant is 290 MB); the publisher states no row count, so expect of order 10^5 award records for 1983-present and a first-time-Phase-I subset for 2005-2018 in the tens of thousands of firms, i.e. a released table well under 50 MB.
construction.format: Single comma-separated CSV (UTF-8) served as a direct HTTP download; an equivalent JSON API exists but exposes fewer award fields.
construction.source_examples: Documented value checks from the Awards Data Dictionary: phase is '1' or '2' without quotes; program is 'SBIR' or 'STTR'; award_year is a 4-digit federal fiscal year; state is 2 characters from the USPS state list; number_employees is a whole number in the range 0-500; hubzone_owned, women_owned and socially_economically_disadvantaged are each 'Y', 'N' or 'U'; proposal_award_date and contract_end_date are YYYY-MM-DD and mandatory except for HHS.

evidence.claim: SBA publishes the complete award corpus as a direct download, with the no-abstract file at 65 MB
evidence.quote: Every SBIR/STTR award since the program’s inception is available for download.

evidence.claim: Field-level definitions and permitted values for every column used, including the Phase code and the award date semantics
proposal_award_date is the first day of performance and is mandatory only for agencies other than HHS, which is why the cohort is an award year
evidence.quote: The first day of contract performance

evidence.claim: Statutory basis: copyright does not subsist in works of the U.S. Government within the United States
evidence.quote: Copyright protection under this title is not available for any work of the United States Government

evidence.claim: SBA establishes and maintains the award databases as a statutory function, which is why the compilation is a U.S. Government work
evidence.quote: SBA establishes databases and websites to collect and maintain, in a common format, information that is necessary to assist SBCs and assess the SBIR/STTR programs.

evidence.claim: Phase II is defined as further development of Phase I work, i.e. the outcome is a genuine stage gate rather than a clerical field
evidence.quote: Phase II awards to further develop work from Phase I that meets particular program needs and exhibits potential for commercial application.

limitations: SBIR.gov is agency-reported and uneven across agencies and years; award_amount and number_employees are as-published values that may have been corrected after the award, so this is a current-vintage retrospective extract and not a snapshot of what an analyst saw on the award date.

There is no parent key linking a Phase II to its Phase I, so conversion is inferred from firm identifier, agency and award-year window; a small share of labels will be misassigned, for example when a repeat awardee's later Phase II is credited to the wrong Phase I.
Firm identity depends on UEI, DUNS or name matching, and DUNS is an optional field in the dictionary, so some firms may be merged or split across identifiers.
HHS awards omit proposal_award_date by design ('Yes, Except HHS' in the dictionary), so the decision instant is a fiscal year rather than an exact date for NIH awardees.
17 U.S.C. §105(a) is territorial: it removes copyright within the United States only and does not establish public-domain status elsewhere; downstream reuse outside the US needs its own analysis.
Award titles and abstracts are company-authored text and are excluded from the release rather than relicensed.
Phase III commercialisation data sit in a government-only database under the Policy Directive, so the observable horizon stops at the Phase II stage gate.
Firms whose first Phase I award falls after 2018 are excluded because their four-year outcome window is not closed at the freeze.
reason: SBIR.gov publishes one 65 MB CSV containing every SBIR/STTR award since 1983, listing both phases. Because Phase I and Phase II records sit in the same file, a first-time Phase I award can be labelled by whether the same firm receives a Phase II award from the same agency within four award-years. That is a recorded event no column states directly, it is uncensored once cohorts end four years before the file's last award year, and one row per firm (its first-ever award record) keeps observations independent and supports clean chronological splits by award year. The only weakness is licensing: SBA grants no licence, so reuse rests on 17 U.S.C. §105(a), which I verified, together with SBA's own statement that it establishes and maintains these databases and publishes every award for download. Company-authored abstract text is excluded from the release to preserve third-party rights.

task.decision_user: An SBIR programme analyst or the awardee firm's leadership, at the point the Phase I award is announced, deciding whether to plan, staff and budget a Phase II proposal.

task.outcome_horizon: Up to four federal fiscal years after the Phase I award year.
task.population: Firms whose earliest award record in the frozen SBIR.gov no-abstract file is a Phase I award with award_year from 2005 through 2018 and a resolvable firm key: UEI, else DUNS, else normalized company name plus state. Firms with any earlier award record of either phase, or whose earliest record is Phase II, are excluded. Each firm contributes one row; same-year multiple Phase I records are included only when proposal_award_date identifies a unique earliest record.
task.prediction_time: The Phase I award date: proposal_award_date when published and inside the federal fiscal year of award_year; otherwise the fiscal year end of award_year. Only fields on the index Phase I award record are read.
task.question: Will a firm's first-ever SBIR/STTR Phase I award convert into a Phase II award from the same agency within four fiscal years?
task.simple_references: Majority-class rate within each split; agency-by-award-year conversion base rate. Persistence is not available because each firm appears once and has no prior Phase I outcome to carry forward.
task.split_policy: Chronological on Phase I award_year, fixed before any measurement: train 2005-2014, eval 2015-2016, holdout 2017-2018. No embargo is applied, because every feature is read from the Phase I record at its own award year and no label value is ever an input; the only timing rule is that each row's four-year window (ending at most 2022 for the 2018 cohort) must be closed inside the frozen file.
task.target: 1 if the same firm (matched on UEI, else DUNS, else normalised company name plus state) has any Phase II record from the same agency with award_year in {y+1, y+2, y+3, y+4}, where y is the Phase I award_year; 0 if no such record exists in the frozen file. Rows are dropped when no firm identifier can be resolved or when y+4 exceeds the last complete award year in the file.
task.usefulness: No source column records Phase I to Phase II conversion, so the label must be rebuilt by linking a later Phase II award to the same firm and agency. Conversion is the SBIR stage gate, and raw Phase I and Phase II counts are confounded by firm survival and agency differences, so within-agency award-time attributes can add signal.

title: Stage-gate conversion of first-time SBIR/STTR Phase I awards to Phase II: will a new awardee firm advance within four years?
